title: EMA Environmental Risk Assessment for Generic and Hybrid Applications: Requirements and Precedents for Relying on Existing Data
summary: How EMA applies ERA requirements to generic and hybrid applications, and when existing assessments, literature or exposure arguments can replace new studies.
body_markdown:
## EMA environmental risk assessment for generic and hybrid applications: requirements and precedents for relying on existing data


### Key points


- Generic (Article 10(1)), hybrid (Article 10(3)) and similar biological (Article 10(4)) applications are not exempt from submitting an environmental risk assessment (ERA). The 2024 Revision 1 of EMA's human-medicines ERA guideline says this explicitly[115](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=115) .
- Submitting an ERA is not the same as submitting new studies. Since the 2006 guideline, EMA has accepted that the absence of ERA studies can be justified for generics, provided the justification addresses any possible significant increase in environmental exposure[140](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=140)[141](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=141) .
- Revision 1 adds a generic-specific route. Repeat studies are generally not required where an EU authority has already found a relevant ERA satisfactory and the applicant justifies why its conclusions still apply. Using another company's data, however, still requires written consent or a letter of access[143](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=143)[505](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=505)[506](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=506) .
- Published literature can replace or supplement recommended studies if it is reliable (CRED categories 1 or 2) and of comparable design. Public assessment reports and regulatory summaries do not count as ERA dossier data[90](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=90)[91](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=91)[92](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=92) .
- EPAR precedents fall into three groups. Exposure-substitution justifications are routinely accepted for generics. Prevalence- or consumption-refined Phase I calculations and public-domain data have also been accepted. Literature-based arguments without study reports or real data have been rejected; CHMP has then required post-authorisation study commitments, or the application was withdrawn before a conclusion.


### Legal basis and regulatory status of the ERA


EMA's guideline describes the obligation under Article 8(3) of Directive 2001/83/EC this way: "the evaluation of the potential environmental risks posed by medicinal products should be submitted, their environmental impact should be assessed and, on a case-by-case basis, specific arrangements to limit it should be envisaged. In any event this impact should not constitute a criterion for refusal of a marketing authorisation"[117](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=117) . The ERA is required for initial EU marketing authorisation applications regardless of legal basis and is filed in Module 1.6[114](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=114)[115](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=115)[116](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=116) . EMA guidance also states that ERA outcome is not a ground for refusal[117](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=117)[118](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=118) .


The applicable EMA documents are:


Document Date

Questions and answers on the ERA guideline, first version 11 April 2011[311](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=311)


Questions and answers on the ERA guideline, Revision 1 (EMA/CHMP/SWP/44609/2010) 2 June 2016, adopted by CHMP 26 May 2016[310](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=310)[144](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=144)[288](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=288)


Draft guideline, Revision 1 December 2018[305](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=305)


Guideline on the ERA of medicinal products for human use, Revision 1 1 September 2024[301](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=301)


#### The tiered assessment in brief


- **Phase I.** The surface-water predicted environmental concentration (PECsw) is calculated as maximum daily dose × market penetration factor (Fpen) ÷ (wastewater per inhabitant per day × dilution factor)[292](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=292) . The default Fpen, wastewater volume and dilution factor are 0.01, 200 L/inhabitant/day and 10, respectively[293](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=293) . Below 0.01 µg/L, with no other concern, risk is considered unlikely. At or above that limit, Phase II follows. The limit may not apply to substances that can affect reproduction at lower concentrations[294](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=294) .
- **PBT/vPvB screening.** All active substances are screened regardless of PEC. A log Kow above 4.5 triggers a definitive PBT/vPvB assessment[124](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=124)[125](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=125) .
- **Phase II.** Tier A compares PECsw with the predicted no-effect concentration (PNEC) using physico-chemical, fate and ecotoxicity studies. Where a risk is identified, Tier B refines exposure and, if warranted, effects[123](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=123) . Under Revision 1, some substance groups enter Phase II irrespective of PEC, and some need tailored testing[122](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=122) .


### How EMA applies the ERA to Article 10 applications


#### No exemption, but studies can be justified away


Under Revision 1 (heading "Q2a: Does the application refer to Article 10 of Directive 2001/83/EC?"), "Applications under Art 10(1)-generic medicinal products, Art 10(3)-hybrid and Art 10(4)-similar biological applications … are not exempt from submitting an ERA". The same applies to Article 10a well-established use, 10b fixed combination and 10c informed consent applications[115](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=115) .


The 2006 guideline already allowed for this: "There may be cases in which the absence of ERA studies could be justified (e.g. marketing authorisation applications for generic medicinal products or type II variations)". The rationale must take account of any possible significant increase in environmental exposure[140](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=140)[141](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=141) . The 2016 Q&A states that suitable evidence of no significant increase in exposure can justify the absence of a complete ERA. It suggests active-ingredient consumption data over time as useful evidence and allows other convincing arguments for a generic[144](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=144)[145](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=145) . The Q&A also confirms that a generic applicant cannot cross-reference the originator's ERA without the originator's consent[289](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=289)[290](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=290) .


#### When a generic or hybrid may increase exposure


The Q&A gives these cautions:


- A generic may increase exposure, for example if it is launched in a Member State where the reference product is not marketed[146](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=146) .
- For type II variations and line extensions, a new ERA is needed if increased exposure is expected. Examples are a larger patient population, a new indication, a higher maximum recommended dose, or a formulation (such as a patch) that retains significant drug substance after use. Significance is judged case by case[147](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=147) .


These triggers matter most for hybrids, which by definition differ from the reference product (for example in strength, dosage form, route or indication).


#### Revision 1, Q2b: earlier ERAs for the same active substance


Revision 1 sets out how an applicant should handle prior ERA data:


- The ERA is product-specific and remains the applicant's responsibility, even where an earlier ERA exists for the same active substance[505](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=505) .
- Data sharing is encouraged, particularly to avoid animal studies. Another MAH's study reports may be submitted with the data owner's written consent[505](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=505) .
- If sharing is not agreed, the applicant must still provide a complete ERA. **Specifically for generics** , repeating studies will generally not be required where an EU national competent authority found a relevant ERA satisfactory and the applicant justifies why its scientific conclusions apply to the generic. The generic's SmPC and package leaflet should then carry information and risk-mitigation measures aligned with that ERA[143](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=143) . The Q2b passage does not expressly extend this route to hybrids[143](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=143) .
- If the earlier ERA is incomplete against current standards (missing studies, or possible increased exposure), the applicant should perform the missing studies and/or update the ERA[507](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=507)[508](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=508) .
- Where risk cannot be excluded, or the substance is PBT/vPvB, the SmPC should reflect this and the applicant should propose measures to limit environmental impact[509](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=509)[510](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=510) .


#### Naturally occurring substances


Vitamins, electrolytes, amino acids, peptides, proteins, nucleotides, carbohydrates and lipids are not exempt. However, their ERA may consist of a justification for not submitting studies, for example on physicochemical or environmental-fate grounds. Herbal products are treated in a similar way[120](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=120)[142](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=142)[121](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=121) .


### Using published literature and existing data instead of new studies


Revision 1's sections on publicly available data and on evaluation of studies set the conditions:


- For an already marketed active substance, the applicant should provide a complete literature review so that relevant existing data are used and animal studies are not repeated. Study reports and peer-reviewed literature must contain enough detail to assess reliability[89](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=89) .
- Published studies of acceptable quality may replace or supplement recommended experimental studies, support a tailored assessment, or update an ERA obtained from another MAH. The applicant should document the search, list relevant studies with their reliability scores, and make sure that any literature study used in place of a recommended study has a comparable design. Published studies need not be GLP-compliant[90](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=90) .
- Reliability and relevance should be assessed consistently using a standardised method such as CRED. Only CRED categories 1 and 2 may be used in the risk assessment. Categories 3 and 4 may not[91](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=91) .
- PARs, EPARs and reviews or summary data from other regulatory frameworks are not ERA dossier data in themselves. Using another company's endpoints requires a letter of access, and the applicant should hold and submit the underlying study reports. Older endpoints, or endpoints assessed under different standards, may not meet current requirements[92](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=92) . A prior assessment under REACH or another framework therefore does not by itself exempt a substance from fate or ecotoxicity testing[92](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=92)[93](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=93) .


### EPAR precedents


The examples below come from EMA EPARs. Unless an EPAR states the legal basis, the application type is given only as far as the cited passage supports it.


#### 1. Exposure-substitution justification accepted (no ERA studies)


This is the most common approach for centrally authorised generics. The standard wording is that the product "is considered unlikely to result in any significant increase in the combined sales volumes" and environmental exposure, so "the ERA is expected to be similar".


Product (substance) Application type in EPAR Outcome


Amlodipine/Valsartan Mylan (amlodipine/valsartan) Generic, Article 10(1)[60](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=60) Sales expected to replace similar products, with no increase in exposure[61](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=61)


Leflunomide medac (leflunomide) Generic[41](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=41) No ERA presented. The exposure justification "was agreed by the CHMP"[40](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=40)


Ebilfumin (oseltamivir) Generic[54](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=54) "The CHMP agreed with this justification"[53](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=53)


Ribavirin Mylan (ribavirin) Generic[43](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=43) "A suitable justification for the absence of a formal environmental risk assessment has been provided"[42](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=42)


Emtricitabine/Tenofovir disoproxil Mylan Generic[58](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=58) Justification also relied on pharmaceutical equivalence to Truvada[59](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=59)


Levetiracetam Teva, Sitagliptin Accord, Azacitidine Mylan, Bortezomib Sun, Zoledronic acid Teva Generics Generic[34](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=34)[68](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=68)[50](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=50)[52](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=52)[56](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=56) Standard sales-volume justification[33](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=33)[69](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=69)[49](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=49)[51](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=51)[55](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=55)


DuoResp Spiromax (budesonide/formoterol) Hybrid[273](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=273) "The justification for the absence of an environmental risk assessment (ERA) is acceptable and an ERA is not deemed necessary"[623](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=623)[624](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=624)


Vylaer Spiromax (budesonide/formoterol) Hybrid application (same assessment language)[626](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=626) Justification accepted[627](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=627)


Kigabeq (vigabatrin) Article 10(3) hybrid[580](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=580) Phase I/II not justified because use was expected to redistribute rather than increase. The applicant committed to reassess if it marketed the product in a country where vigabatrin was not already marketed[580](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=580)


The Kigabeq commitment applies the Q&A caution about launches in Member States without the reference product[146](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=146) .


#### 2. Refined Phase I using consumption or prevalence data


Some generic and hybrid applicants calculated a Phase I PEC instead of relying only on a substitution argument. They used real consumption or prevalence data to refine Fpen.


- **Trabectedin Accord (generic):** European consumption data and published epidemiology refined exposure. PECsw fell below the action limit, and there was no non-clinical objection[225](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=225)[226](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=226) .
- **Teriflunomide Viatris (generic):** Annual consumption and European prevalence data supported Phase I. Phase II was unnecessary and the ERA was acceptable[227](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=227)[228](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=228) .
- **Nordimet (methotrexate, hybrid):** A prevalence-based Phase I gave a PECsw below 0.01 µg/L, so Phase II was not needed[579](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=579)[565](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=565) .
- **Puldysa (idebenone, hybrid):** The applicant was asked to recalculate PEC using prevalence for the current indication and 100% market share. The revised PEC was below 0.01 µg/L and drew on environmental data from the applicant's earlier dossier[577](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=577)[578](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=578) .
- **Teriparatide Sun (hybrid):** Phase I PECsw of 0.0001 µg/L. No further assessment was needed[567](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=567)[568](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=568)[569](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=569) .


#### 3. Public-domain and literature data accepted


- **Fulvestrant Mylan (fulvestrant):** Public-domain physicochemical, bioconcentration, aquatic toxicity and environmental-fate data, together with known metabolism, supported the case that Phase II was not required. This held despite fulvestrant's potential as an endocrine disruptor[221](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=221)[490](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=490) . The ERA was judged acceptable[491](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=491) . The cited passages do not state the legal basis[489](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=489) .
- **Tuzulby (methylphenidate, hybrid):** PEC exceeded the action limit in some countries. Published information supported a conclusion that no environmental risk was expected, although no ecotoxicity data were available to derive a PNEC. The applicant was reminded to complete the ERA under the revised guideline, and the product was considered approvable[553](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=553)[574](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=574) .
- **Doxorubicin Hydrochloride Tillomed (hybrid):** A PEC of 0.45 µg/L triggered Phase II. A published *Daphnia magna* -derived PNEC gave a PEC/PNEC below 1[223](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=223)[224](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=224) . The application was withdrawn, and no CHMP ERA conclusion is recorded[201](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=201) .
- **Sancuso (granisetron, hybrid):** The MAH was recommended to perform a literature-based Phase II analysis covering patch use and disposal[572](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=572) . This is consistent with the Q&A's reference to patches that retain drug substance[147](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=147) .


#### 4. Literature or justification not accepted


These cases show where CHMP has drawn the line:


- **Imatinib Koanaa (Article 10(3) hybrid):** PECsw was 4.275 µg/L, well above 0.01 µg/L[270](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=270)[539](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=539) . The applicant argued that sales would be redistributed among imatinib products. CHMP found the argument unsupported by actual data and did not accept it. It requested a full Phase II and an experimental log Kow study report[540](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=540)[541](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=541) . A literature log Kow value had been supplied without a study report[570](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=570) . There was no non-clinical objection, subject to a post-authorisation commitment to submit the ERA studies[542](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=542) .
- **Efmody (hydrocortisone):** The applicant cited literature on ready biodegradability to avoid tailored Phase II studies. CHMP did not accept the published reference[515](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=515) . It recommended a ready biodegradability test and the protocol or literature supporting the log Kow value post-authorisation[516](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=516) . CHMP did accept reliance on literature for non-clinical safety[514](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=514) .
- **Pravafenix (fenofibrate/pravastatin):** An ERA based on bibliographic references for both substances was considered not yet acceptable[230](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=230) .
- **Diractin (ketoprofen):** An ERA based on published data was incomplete and could not rule out risk or the need for Phase II. The application was withdrawn[246](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=246)[199](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=199) .
- **Qtrilmet (metformin/saxagliptin/dapagliflozin):** Existing single-substance ERAs and a published review of metformin fate were reused. Newer literature on possible effects on fish reproduction led CHMP to recommend a fish reproduction study post-approval[231](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=231) .
- **Taxotere (docetaxel, indication extension):** Fate and effects information was supplied without study reports, along with literature log Kow values. CHMP found this inadequate, and the MAH made commitments on bioaccumulation testing and a Phase II ERA[244](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=244)[245](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=245) .


### Practical lessons for generic and hybrid applicants


1. **Always file Module 1.6.** A justification is an ERA. Leaving the section empty is not[115](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=115)[144](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=144) .
2. **Support substitution claims with data.** Standard sales-volume wording has been widely accepted for straightforward generics[40](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=40)[53](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=53)[61](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=61) . Imatinib Koanaa shows CHMP can reject the argument when PEC is high and no real data back the claim[540](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=540)[541](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=541) .
3. **Check hybrid differences against the Q&A triggers:** new indication or population, higher maximum dose, new Member State markets, and formulations such as patches[146](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=146)[147](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=147) . Refined Phase I calculations using prevalence or consumption data have been an effective middle path[227](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=227)[579](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=579)[577](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=577) .
4. **Qualify literature properly.** Score reliability (CRED 1 or 2), show comparable study design, and do not rely on EPARs or regulatory summaries as data[90](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=90)[91](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=91)[92](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=92) . Literature log Kow values without study reports have repeatedly been challenged[570](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=570)[516](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=516)[244](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=244) .
5. **Plan for data access early.** Cross-referencing another company's ERA requires consent or a letter of access[289](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=289)[506](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=506) . Without it, the Revision 1 Q2b route for generics depends on a satisfactory prior EU assessment and a scientific bridging justification[143](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=143) .
6. **Expect post-authorisation commitments rather than refusal.** ERA is not a refusal criterion[117](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=117) . Gaps are normally closed through commitments to submit studies after approval[542](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=542)[516](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=516)[231](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/ema-environmental-risk-assessment-for-generic?showSourceNumber=231) .
